title: Conversation econ — weighted scenarios lab
content:
Quick reminder: this is a personal scratchpad for thinking about conversation-weighted pricing. Not for publishing yet — lots of rough numbers and TODOs.

Goal: produce a simple hybrid pricing proposal that (a) captures value from long, engaged sessions; (b) doesn't punish tiny bursts; (c) is robust to caching and batching improvements; (d) easy to explain to sales.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline model serving cost (platform-level, after infra optimizations) = $3.00 / GPU-hour (effective, amortized across multi-tenant) — conservative for a mixed fleet.
- Per-GPU sustained token output for typical chat model (mixed prompt+gen) = 3,000 tokens/sec (this is optimistic for smaller models, pessimistic for huge ones; we use it to get lower-bound token cost).
  - Tokens/hour/GPU = 3,000 * 3600 = 10.8M tokens/hr.
- Raw infra cost per token = $3 / 10.8M = $0.0000002778 ~= $2.78e-7 / token. (call it 2.8e-7)
- Add overhead (control plane, storage, monitoring, SRE, licensing): multiply by 3x -> $8.4e-7 / token (~$0.00000084).
- Add margin / product ops / sales: target unit price ~ 6x infra -> $1.68e-6 / token (~$0.00000168).
- Rounded consumer-facing payg baseline: $0.0000017 / token (this is ~ $1.7 per million tokens).

Reality checks:
- If throughput is lower (e.g., 1,000 tps), infra cost/token triples -> product price would need to be ~ $0.005 / 1k tokens? re-calc. Keep in mind that model size matters a lot; these numbers are only for medium models on modern GPUs with batching and KV cache.

Session math (to connect to product ideas):
- Typical short message session: 2 turns, 100 tokens input + 150 tokens output = 250 tokens / session. Cost @ $0.0000017 = $0.000425 / session (~0.0425¢).
- Typical engaged session: 10 turns, average 120 tokens per turn (prompt+response) = 1,200 tokens. Cost = $0.00204 / session (~0.204¢).
- Heavy assistant session (research): 60 turns, average 250 tokens = 15,000 tokens -> cost = $0.0255 / session (~2.55¢).

Cache impact / reuse: (important for chat)
- If we cache prefixes / retrieved context (KV cache reuse), the marginal tokens to generate later turns drop substantially. Example: 10-turn convo where first turn consumes 2,000 tokens (long system + user) then each follow-up requires only 200 tokens. Weighted tokens: 2,000 + 9*200 = 3,800 tokens vs naive 10*1200 = 12,000. Big delta.
- Practical cache hit assumptions: 50–80% reuse for assistant-heavy apps; for code-assistant sessions maybe 30–50%.
- Implication: pricing purely per-token over-incentivizes chat apps to re-architect for caching (good) but also compresses revenue for long sessions — need to capture session-level value.

Two-layer hybrid idea (simple and explainable):
1) Base subscription (per-seat or per-app): includes a pool of monthly included sessions and a small token buffer for misc API calls.
2) Pay-as-you-go tokens above buffer at $0.0000017 / token.
3) Session surcharge for long-running conversations (session-credits) that amortize cold-start costs and incentivize efficient workloads: e.g., any session with > 2,500 tokens consumes 1 session-credit; > 10k tokens consumes 5 credits. Credits priced to reflect amortized connection + KV cold fill + tracing cost (approx $0.01/credit).

Rationale:
- Small bursts (most of our users) pay only token rate or are covered by included token buffer.
- Long sessions (which consume more infra-heavy state, longer KV warm-up, more tracing) pay a small fixed surcharge that recovers fixed costs and lets us offer lower marginal token price.
- Session credits are easy to show on invoices and explain: "You get X included sessions per seat; heavy sessions use credits."

Backtests / scenario sims (cohorts):
- Cohort A: 10k monthly users, median sessions/user = 8, mean tokens/session = 300 (mostly short).
  - Monthly tokens = 10k*8*300 = 24M tokens -> revenue @ $1.7/M = $40.8 (~$0.0000017*24M = $40.8). That seems tiny; implies our per-token price must be much higher for any meaningful revenue unless seat/subscription layer exists.
- Cohort B: 500 midmarket seats, each 1k sessions/month, mean 1,500 tokens/session = 750M tokens -> raw token revenue = $1,275 (again small!).
-> Conclusion: token-only pricing at consumer-level needs much higher per-token price or must be combined with seat or commitment to reach enterprise economics. This matches typical vendor observations.

Alternative: session-bundles model (simple packs):
- Sell packs: 1,000 session-credits = $X. Each credit covers up to 2,500 tokens; overage billed at token rate. Price idea: $0.01 / credit -> 1k credits = $10. Practical: allows easy bundling for midmarket.

Edge cases & gameability:
- Customers could split a long convo into many short ones to avoid credits; but that imposes friction and degrades UX (so probably limited).
- They could reduce prompt size to move cost into token band — which is OK, encourages efficiency.
- Bots that stream tokens forever (open-ended) — protect with session caps and per-session throttle after N tokens.

Open TODOs / experiments to run: 
- Run traffic sample through platform telemetry and compute real effective tokens-per-gpu-hour across fleet (by model family). Use that to calibrate per-token infra cost. (Metric: tokens_out_total / gpu_hours_total, segmented by model and sequence length).
- Compute observed cache-reuse distribution per session length buckets. We need percentiles (p50/p90/p99) of marginal token counts after caching.
- A/B test session-credit framing: $0.01/credit vs $0.02/credit vs no credit (higher token price) — measure conversion and churn.
- Simulate revenue for a mixed book-of-business: 60% short sessions (p300), 35% medium (p1200), 5% long (p10k) and compare pure-token vs hybrid vs seat+token.

Notes to self (sales messaging bullets):
- "Predictable bills for heavy users — keep the token price low, pay a small fixed for very big conversations."
- "Session credits amortize complexity (cold starts, traces, long-lived KV) and make per-conversation pricing sensible for embedded assistants."
- "Small teams get generous included short sessions with payg tokens for spike usage."

Small worked example (seller cheat-sheet):
- 1 seat, Starter plan = $29/mo -> includes 1,000 sessions (up to 2,500 tokens each) + 500k tokens buffer. Extra tokens = $1.7 per million. Extra credits = $0.01 each (1 credit covers session >2.5k tokens).
- If team has 200 sessions/mo at avg 600 tokens -> consumption = 120k tokens, covered easily by buffer. If 10 sessions are heavy (12k tokens), they consume 10*5=50 credits -> $0.50. Simple to explain.

Risks:
- Complexity: session-credits + token-rate might be confusing at first. Keep UI/console clarity high.
- Accounting: need to ensure billing shows both token and session credit usage per customer and per-route.

Final-ish thoughts:
- Pure token pricing is simple but economically thin; subscription + token + small session surcharge seems to balance predictability and fairness.
- Key next step: calibrate with real infra telemetry (urgent). Then run a small pilot with 10 SMB customers on hybrid plan.

Random notes / brainstorming:
- Could offer a "warmth" metric per session that accounts for prefix reuse; charge less for warm sessions (i.e., discounted token rate for high prefix reuse). Hard to explain but powerful.
- Offer burst credits for interactive web apps: 1 free burst per user/day, or a shared pool.

TODO list (short):
- [ ] Get tokens_per_gpu_hour by model family (eng infra ask).
- [ ] Instrument chat API to report pre-cache vs post-cache marginal tokens per call (eng).
- [ ] Build revenue sim using cohorts and new hybrid pricing (finance/growth).
- [ ] Mock UI billing screens for session credits (design/product).

End of scratchpad. Feel free to copy into PRD when cleaned up.
